description.p: Schedule and run PowerShell scripts and console processes from an Avalonia desktop UI. The same program runs as the Windows service or systemd unit. Register it, edit schedules, and follow logs without a browser.
The Flatpak is the desktop window. Script files and logs live under the home folder. Register the service on the host when scripts must keep running with nobody signed in.

ul.li: Script list, schedules, and log viewing
Register, start, and stop the service (prompts for elevation)
Windows and Linux script compatibility flags
After an upgrade, What's New lists additions since the version you last opened
Keep a console program running under the service, and start or stop it from the Processes tab

description.p: The Processes tab keeps console programs running under the service. The window remembers its size and position.
The desktop program is the service. Launch runs a script now. What's New lists additions since the version you last opened.
Unhandled UI errors open a copyable dialog and are saved to a crash log. Windows setup keeps an existing desktop shortcut on reinstall.
Linux Flatpak uses X11/XWayland from the GNOME app icon and a lowercase app id.
